question: Derive the frequency response of a discrete time system.
_instructions: For each step set 'human_correct' to true/false. Set 'error_type' to one of: algebra, sign, missing_term, substitution, definition, none. Set '_filled' to true when done. Set 'final_answer_correct' to true/false after comparing 'generated_final' to 'expected_final'.

steps.description: Start with a linear time-invariant discrete-time system described by its impulse response h[n]
steps.notes: Valid starting point for LTI system characterization.

steps.description: The output y[n] is the convolution of input x[n] and impulse response h[n]
steps.notes: Standard discrete convolution sum. Correct. parse_fail is a tooling artifact.

steps.description: Assume the input is a complex exponential x[n] = exp(I*Omega*n)
steps.notes: Standard eigenfunction input for LTI systems. Correct.

steps.description: Substitute the input into the convolution sum
Factor out the term that does not depend on k
steps.notes: exp(I*Omega*n) is independent of k and correctly factored out. Remaining sum is over k only.

steps.description: Recognize that the sum is the definition of the discrete-time Fourier transform of h[n]
steps.notes: This is exactly the DTFT definition H(Omega) = sum h[k] exp(-jΩk). Correct identification.

steps.description: Define the frequency response H(Omega) as the DTFT of h[n]
steps.notes: Correct naming of the frequency response.

steps.description: Write the output in terms of the input and frequency response
steps.notes: y[n] = H(Omega)*x[n] confirms complex exponential is an eigenfunction of LTI system. Correct.

steps.description: Express H(Omega) as the z-transform of h[n] evaluated on the unit circle
steps.notes: H(e^jΩ) = H(z)|_{z=e^jΩ}. Standard relationship between Z-transform and DTFT. Correct.

steps.description: If the system is described by a difference equation, take the z-transform of both sides
steps.notes: Valid alternative derivation path via Z-transform. H(z) = Y(z)/X(z) by linearity. Correct.

steps.description: Solve for the transfer function H(z) = Y(z)/X(z)
Evaluate the transfer function on the unit circle to get frequency response
steps.notes: Evaluating H(z) at z = exp(I*Omega) gives the frequency response. Correct final result.
